title: Search performance -  better caching logic for queries on wildcard field

timeline.body:
Remove use of BooleanQuery in WildcardField regex/wildcard/fuzzy/prefix searches to prevent query caching framework from running the contained verification query clauses across whole index at great expense.

The new BinaryDvConfirmedAutomatonQuery provides a replacement wrapper for the approximation and verification clauses that plays better with caching logic

Closes #75848

I think this could perform a full scan in the worst case, because `advance` tries to find the first matching document greater than the doc ID. For example, `verifyDisi` could only match one document, which happens to be the last one `maxDoc - 1`. When we call `advance` on some doc ID, it will step through every document to the end, testing whether it matches.

Looking at `ConjunctionScorer`, I'm not sure we actually need to override its `twoPhaseIterator` method here.

I'm not sure adding this new class is super useful at the moment -- we only have one example right now that fits into this mold. I think it'd be best to just make a targeted fix for `AutomatonQueryOnBinaryDv` as a first iteration. Specifically, maybe this query could take in an approximation query as a parameter, and be renamed to something like `BinaryDvConfirmedAutomatonQuery`?

I suspect that a targeted fix will be clearer and have a lot less boilerplate. We can always follow-up later with a refactor if we encounter more examples of approximation + verification queries?

Mostly a personal preference, but I think it'd be clearer to remove this constructor and force the caller to pass in `MatchAllDocsQuery`. That makes it really clear to the caller this query might do a full scan!

reply.body: I did have it that way before and felt like I was repeating the same code but, agreed, it's probably safer to reiterate the match-all point.

timeline.body: Would it make more sense to assert that `advanceExact` always returns true? It seems like it'd indicate a serious bug in our logic if this returned false.

reply.body: Will add an assertion. We'll still need the if for when running without assertions on.

timeline.body: Do we need to wrap this in a `ConstantScoreQuery`, since this query already uses a `ConstantScoreScorer`?

reply.body: Good point. That was a relic from when we wrapped in a BooleanQuery

timeline.body: This looks good to me! I left some very minor comments.

The new ApproximationAndVerificationQuery provides a replacement wrapper that plays better with caching logic

Closes #75848
